scope: Five-second ComfyUI-native Wan2.2 TI2V 5B motion trials across multiple dinosaur taxa

policy.publicRule: Only independently reviewed safe frames may enter a documented non-looping motion-only derivative.

profileFindings.finding: Official-length native generation produced strong readable motion but accumulated late identity and anatomy drift in all directly reviewed full clips.
Reduced temporal latent length improved some identity retention but often produced insufficient motion, alternating texture pulses, or late rigid-part drift.
Reused accepted source frames without optical-flow synthesis; two non-looping motion-only derivatives passed all-frame review.

trials.review: Neck stayed connected, but frames 46-121 developed skull, rostrum, body-orientation, and shortened hooked-tail drift.
The animal rotated about 180 degrees, feather and head identity smeared, the tail became fan-like, and the breath formed an incorrect vertical column.
The single tail club disappeared from frame 2, a forefoot lifted and replanted, and the background drifted.
Rotation and anatomy improved, but the breath became an oversized persistent white mass extending to the ground.
The arms and head drifted toward a quadrupedal horse-like form despite the no-breath prompt.
Anatomy passed 81 of 81 frames, but head displacement stayed below one pixel and alternating 16 fps micro-jitter made the requested larger motion unreadable.
The head moved only about four pixels while background drift read as a pseudo camera pan.
From frame 24 the rigid tubular crest rotated and grew independently of the skull, causing a clear identity failure.
From frame 19 the rounded nasal mound split and squared off; the tail shortened and hooked and a foreleg bent abnormally.

The full clip failed at frame 73 because the head and nasal mound popped to a different identity. Frames 0-72 retained every required Brachiosaurus cue and were used in a non-interpolated partial reverse return.

The full clip failed when the torso began turning at frame 49 and finger count drifted from frame 52. Frames 0-48 retained the deep skull, two-finger hands, grounded legs, and side-view torso and were used in a settled partial reverse return.
